chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: Publishers' night and song pluggers at rehearsal
summary: Song pluggers attended a weekly rehearsal and left copies; McRae and Ella later went through the songs privately to choose.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: We're in Los Angeles, so the man came up to me and says -- So the next day when I came to work, it was like publishers night -- Tuesday night. And it was about fifteen of these song pluggers standing around trying to get their songs in the book, you know, and on the air.
Publishers night.

Yeah. Like we had song pluggers. You know, back in those days it didn't have a lot of radio or television, (it was just inaudible) records they have to play. You know, like depending on to get your songs on the radio. So all these big companies like Robbins and (Ludo inaudible) and Mills -- the companies had song pluggers in all -- They had offices in California. A band come to town, if they had a hit song (even on the inaudible) road. "Hey, this is our new song," and --
Where did they meet you?
They come out to rehearsal.

Rehearsal?

Rehearsal. We had rehearsal once a week -- twice a week. One week was a -- Tuesday night -- was the Tuesday afternoon was the day that we let the song pluggers come out. The other rehearsals, Thursday, was strictly for Ella and the band. Nobody was allowed there. We would rehearse that day, too, when the song pluggers come out. But then we had a private rehearsal if you wanted to hear your song. You wouldn't hear it in no rehearsal. You'd have to come out and listen to it there. (inaudible) "We're going to put your song on the air next week." We'd get whoever was going to make the arrangements. Maybe if Benny Carter was out there, we'd say, "Benny", (inaudible). If he was out there in California at that time.
You had copies or were they just lead sheets that were passed around?
No, we had arrangements. We
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
never played lead sheets. Arrangements -- big arrangements (inaudible).
No, I'm talking about when the song pluggers came.
Well, when the song plugger come around, he left the arrangement. He left us a couple of piano copies. You know, like a professional copy.
Oh.

After rehearsal, we'd go over -- After rehearsal is over with, what we would do, I would get with the piano player and Ella. I say, "Ella, I got a couple of songs I want you to take a listen to." And Ella would say, "Okay." We would go over to the piano -- everybody's gone. Just the piano and we'd just be going over these songs that we're going to put in the book. And we would run down these songs with Ella, and decide on which ones she was going to do. We had a lot of songs that never made the

book. Sometime we would make the song up and see if we could work it in. You know, like work around to it and see if we could get it in.
But most of the top things that we do -- things that we pull for Ella, were the things that we would make arrangements on right away.
These are the things that are going to go on the air, go in the book right away.
And if you were a song plugger and you brought me out a song -- you brought me "Goodnight My Love," -- oh, I like that.
So we're going to make arrangements. Got to get in here. (Inaudible). We're going to broadcast next Tuesday or next Wednesday, so you can come out then. But you couldn't come to rehearsal.
Because we didn't allow nobody in rehearsal. Rehearsal was strictly for the band and Ella.
When we rehearsed, there wasn't nobody around, (inaudible). Because we would go through all the things that we didn't want a lot of people want to hear. We'd be telling her things that we want
